title: Plan AZ: AI Coding Security & Testing Checkup — Mandatory Before Shipping
summary: Input validation → secret management → dependency audit → automated tests → review checklist
scenario: Best for the final pre-delivery gate — systematically checking AI-generated code for security and quality issues.

steps.title: Input validation & injection protection
steps.detail: List every user input point: URL params, form fields, request bodies, file paths, export filenames. Focus on the three flaws AI code most often ships — XSS (unescaped front-end rendering), SQL injection (string-concatenated queries) and path traversal (user input used to build file paths). Confirm each entry point is validated or escaped, and at minimum rejects invalid input — never rely on client-side validation alone.
steps.tips: Ask Claude to trace where every piece of data coming from a user or request ends up, then confirm each entry has allowlist validation or parameterized queries.

steps.title: Secrets & sensitive information
steps.detail: Check that API keys, tokens and passwords aren't hardcoded in code, in git history, or in logs. Models sometimes write sample secrets or env vars straight into source, and once a secret lands in a repo the damage is permanent. Standard practice: inject via .env + environment variables, gitignore the .env file, and scrub anything already committed from history.
steps.tips: Scan history with git log -p | grep or gitleaks; once a secret leaks, rotation beats deleting the commit.

steps.title: Dependency audit
steps.detail: Run npm audit or a dependency scanner to surface known vulnerabilities and outdated versions. AI-generated dependencies tend to be the latest or whatever the model 'remembers', which may carry known CVEs or be end-of-life. Triage results by severity — fix high/critical first, and when no fix exists, assess the risk or replace the library.
steps.tips: Don't blind-install packages — check download counts, maintenance cadence and author reputation; lock exact versions so transitive dependencies can't silently shift.

steps.title: Automated tests
steps.detail: Write unit tests for critical logic and end-to-end tests for the key business paths. Don't just test the happy path — add edge cases, bad input, insufficient permissions and timeouts. Have the AI generate cases from your code, but manually add the scenarios where 'the user will do the wrong thing'.
steps.tips: Write a failing test first (red), then make it pass (green) — it exposes real problems better than back-filling tests after the fact.

steps.title: Delivery review checklist
steps.detail: Walk a checklist item by item: input validation, secrets, dependency audit, test coverage, access control, error handling and log redaction. Write the conclusion of every item into the delivery notes — who checked, what was found, what risk remains. This turns the 'checkup' into a traceable delivery artifact instead of a formality.
steps.tips: Keep the checklist as a fixed template committed to the repo (e.g. checklist.md) so you reuse it next time and gaps jump out.

pitfalls.title: Only testing the happy path (edges will blow up)
pitfalls.detail: Empty, oversized, invalid and concurrent inputs are where bugs live; a suite that only exercises the happy path makes the error branch run for the first time in production.

pitfalls.title: Hardcoding secrets into code/repo (leaks are permanent)
pitfalls.detail: Once a secret enters git history, deleting the commit doesn't help — the history is still there. On any leak: rotate the secret, scrub history, and check logs and third-party services for exposure.

pitfalls.title: Blind-installing dependencies brings in vulnerabilities (the chain is long)
pitfalls.detail: The dependency chain is long, and one compromised transitive dependency can sink the whole project; vet a package before installing and audit immediately after.

pitfalls.title: All green but critical paths untested (green doesn't mean real)
pitfalls.detail: Good coverage numbers don't mean the critical path is covered; take the single most important user journey and verify it end-to-end, from entry to persistence.
